intended_object: This is the canonical R-algebra map A ⊗_R Aᵒᵖ → End_R(A) that sends a ⊗ b to the endomorphism x ↦ a·x·b. It is the map used to define Azumaya algebras. I took this from the docstring, the module documentation and how `IsAzumaya` uses it.
explanation:
The definition makes A into an `A ⊗[R] Aᵐᵒᵖ`-module with `TensorProduct.Algebra.module`. The two module structures it combines are:
- A acting on itself by left multiplication;
- Aᵐᵒᵖ acting on A by right multiplication (op b • x = x * b).

These two actions commute, so (a ⊗ op b) • x = a * (x * b). The definition then takes `Algebra.lsmul`, which sends each element of `A ⊗[R] Aᵐᵒᵖ` to the endomorphism "multiply by this element". This gives an R-algebra hom from `A ⊗[R] Aᵐᵒᵖ` to `Module.End R A`.

The lemma `AlgHom.mulLeftRight_apply`, right after the definition, confirms the formula a ⊗ b ↦ (x ↦ a * x * b.unop). That is the standard sandwich map. The setting (R a commutative semiring, A any R-algebra over a semiring) is the most general one in which the construction makes sense. Mathlib has `LinearMap.mulLeftRight` (A →ₗ A →ₗ End R A), a bilinear map rather than an algebra hom from the tensor product, so it is not the same object.
